title: Chronicon Continuans Ubi Prosper Desinit
author: Victor Tununensis Episcopus

passages.original: Octob., et Eugenius episcopus Carthaginiensis Ecclesiae, post dira ercmi cxsilia, plurimis afflictionibus poenisque clarus habetur. Hic itaque Ilunericus inter innumerabiles suarum impietatum strages quas in catholicos exercebat, octavo regni sui anno, interioribus cunctis effusis, ut Arius pater ejus, misere vitam finivit. Cui succedit Guntamundus. Regnavil annis 12 : qui nostros protinus de exsilio revocavit.
passages.english: October, and Eugenius, bishop of the Church of Carthage, after cruel exiles in the desert, is held renowned for very many afflictions and punishments. And so this Huneric, amid the countless slaughters of his impieties which he inflicted on the Catholics, in the eighth year of his reign, with all his inward parts poured out, like Arius his father, ended his life wretchedly. Guntamund succeeds him. He reigned 12 years; he at once recalled our people from exile.
passages.notes: The passage begins mid-date: the preceding context gives "8 cal." (eighth day before the Kalends), so the full date is "on the eighth day before the Kalends of October". Scanning errors corrected: "ercmi cxsilia" for "eremi exsilia", "Ilunericus" for "Hunericus" (Huneric), "Regnavil" for "Regnavit". "Arius pater ejus" calls Arius Huneric's "father" in the sense of the founder of his Arian creed.
